The organised premium fashion market attracts domestic brands, international retailers, digital-first companies and marketplace-led private labels, pressuring pricing, customer acquisition costs and market share.
Consumer preferences evolve at an accelerated pace; delays in identifying trends or responding to demand changes may lower sell-through and increase markdowns or inventory carrying costs.
Inaccurate demand forecasting or unexpected market conditions may lead to excess inventory or stock shortages, affecting revenue growth, profitability and working capital efficiency.
Higher discounting levels across the retail sector may pressure gross margins and increase competitive intensity for premium fashion retailers.
Company performance may be influenced by uncertainties in consumer spending patterns, supply chain disruptions, and raw material price volatility, impacting demand, procurement costs and operations.
